design.heading: Web design
paragraphs: Web design is how your website looks and feels: the layout, the colours, the images, and the way visitors find their way around.
We need to diversify ideas, that is, to open ourselves up to options regarding our problem, and then converge ideas, that is, filter ideas and define the possible solution.

included.text: I can be very creative if I put my mind on it. Use brainstorming to support the creative process.
find unconventional alternatives for your needs.
use mind maps, sticky notes, and other tools to brainstorm solutions.
sort the proposals and check if they align with your business idea.
use adhesive dots or impact matrices to choose the most promising options.

development.heading: Web development
paragraphs: Web development is the building of your website: turning the design into the code that runs in your visitor's browser.

I build with Astro, a modern framework trusted for some of the fastest websites online. That makes your site quick to load, safe, and easy to look after for years to come. And it's yours from day one, with the code, the domain, and the hosting all in your name.

included.text: built with Astro, Laravel, Vue.js, and/or Spring Boot the frameworks behind some of the fastest static and dynamic websites online.
one that stays safe and keeps working, year after year.
the code, the domain, and the hosting all in your name from day one.
space to add new pages and features whenever your business needs them.

sqa.heading: Software Quality Control (SQA)
paragraphs: Software quality assurance (SQA) is the work that keeps your website functioning as, when, and where you need it to, preventing problems before they occur.
I anticipate problems, review development processes, verify and validate software, and apply continuous improvement processes so your website will function almost forever according to your needs.

included.text: software problems can happen, but they are more common if there are no work standards, coding guidelines, methodologies, and a proper description of the needs of your business, users, and customers.
it is necessary to verify the software meets technical requirements and user needs throughout the entire process and it meets the needs of your business.
analyse metrics and error reports to adjust team processes
proactively verify that the solution works.

faq.heading: Questions and answers (freelance working)
faq.lead: The things clients ask before we start.

items.question: What does a website cost?
items.answer: Every project gets one fixed price, agreed before we start. No hourly billing, no surprises afterwards. The free talk — and the free check, if there's already a website — tells me what your project needs, and you get the price in one clear proposal.

items.question: How long does a project take?
items.answer: That depends on the size of the website. The proposal names the timeline together with the price, so you know both before we start.

items.question: What happens with my current website?
items.answer: It stays online until the new one is ready. Your content, your web address, and your Google rankings come along. I check your current website before our first talk, so you get clear answers from the start.

items.question: Do I need to arrange hosting or a domain?
items.answer: No. I set up the hosting and the domain for you, in your own name. If you already have a domain, we simply keep it.

items.question: Do we need to meet in person?
items.answer: It's not needed. Most projects run entirely by phone, video, and email. Currently, I am working with clients locally in Bogota (Colombia).

items.question: Are you a company or agency?
items.answer: I'm a one-person business: a freelancer, not an agency. You work directly with the person doing the work, from the first talk to the finished website. No sales team, no account managers, no handoffs.

items.question: Can I change the website myself after launch?
items.answer: You can simply send me your changes, and the monthly care plan (if we agree) exists exactly for that. If you want to edit the website yourself, say so in the first talk and I set the site up for it.

items.question: Do you also build webshops?
items.answer: No. Big online shops are the one thing I don't build. Everything else that needs a custom Astro, Laravel, Vue.js, and/or a Spring Boot website, I build: tell me in the first talk what you have in mind, and I'll be honest about whether I'm the right builder for it.

items.question: Is the website really mine?
items.answer: Completely. The domain, the hosting, and the code are in your name from day one. If you ever want to move on, you take everything with you: you're never locked in.

items.question: What happens if something breaks after launch?
items.answer: Very little can break if the website is build with Astro: the website has no plugins and no database to fail. And I stay reachable after launch; for regular updates and monitoring there is the monthly care plan. If the website is build with Laravel, Vue.js or Spring Boot, there are more things can go wrong, but the care plan, if we agree, can fix any issue too, verifying databases, services, dependencies, runtime errors, etc.
